sections.html:
A Bucks County house is taxed three ways: by the township or borough, by the school district and by the county. Each levy is the assessed value times that year's millage rate, so one parcel can carry three separate charges. County and township bills go out in early March. School district bills follow in early July.

New construction or another change in assessment triggers an interim bill. Interim bills come quarterly on top of the two annual ones. Every municipality has its own elected tax collector, and the county keeps an online directory of them.

Assessed value is set by a different office. The three-member Board of Assessment Appeals determines market value for each parcel, prepares the tax rolls, keeps the tax maps, assigns parcel numbers and labels documents headed for recording. Millage is decided by the taxing bodies, not by the Board.

Bucks is a large, mostly suburban county on the Delaware River, and home prices run well above those in the state's rural counties. It covers 622 square miles with Doylestown as the seat. Lower Bucks is flat and close to Philadelphia and Trenton, while Upper Bucks is hillier farm and village country. Newer building has pushed north through Middletown, Lower Makefield, Northampton and Newtown.

Figures for 2020 to 2024 show 249,187 households, a median home value of $445,700, median household income of $114,764 and an owner-occupied rate of 77.8%. Median gross rent is $1,605. With values at that level, a tax line on a settlement statement deserves a close read, and new construction nearby can bring interim assessments to neighbors.

File an appeal form with the Board of Assessment Appeals, 55 East Court Street, 6th floor, Doylestown. The filing fee is $75.00 per parcel and is non-refundable. The annual deadline falls in early August and is counted by postmark or office receipt. In 2026 it was August 3. A change won in that round applies the following tax year. Check the county's appeal page each summer for the next date.

Residential appeals follow written rules. Faxed filings are rejected, and a late form is untimely. You, or an attorney holding your signed authorization, must attend the hearing unless you sign a waiver on the form.

  • Evidence of value can be a Pennsylvania certified appraisal that meets USPAP, or sales within the last 18 months of similar homes in your neighborhood.
  • If you bought within 18 months, attach your settlement sheet. It can't be your only evidence.
  • The hearing notice is mailed 20 days ahead, and postponements are refused.
  • A no-show counts as abandoning the appeal, and the fee stays with the county.
  • Group appeals must go through an attorney.

The Board meets on the first and third Tuesday of each month at 10 a.m. at the courthouse in Doylestown. Interim appeals, which follow a revision notice, use the deadline printed on the notice and carry the same $75.00 fee.

School districts cut the assessed value of an owner's primary residence through the homestead exclusion. Farm buildings on at least ten contiguous acres can qualify for a farmstead exclusion. For the school tax year that starts July 1, 2027, the application is due to the Board of Assessment Appeals by March 1, 2027. If no form arrived in the mail, download one from the county's page.

You may be asked to prove residency with a driver's license, voter registration or a tax return. A false statement can cost you back taxes with interest, a 10% penalty on the unpaid tax and a fine of up to $2,500. Each year by December 31, school districts must notify an owner whose approval is expiring or was denied.

Older and disabled owners should also look at the state Property Tax/Rent Rebate Program. It pays $380 to $1,000 depending on income and requires household income of $48,110 or less. The deadline for the 2025 claim year is December 31, 2026. The Department of Revenue's help line is 1-888-222-9190.

Unpaid taxes become a lien, and after 18 months the Tax Claim Bureau can sell the property. Local collectors pass delinquent accounts to the Bureau after December 31, and the Bureau mails a Notice of Claim, usually by certified mail the following spring. The lien is automatic and shows in the public record with no filing at the prothonotary.

The upset sale happens in September of the second year after the first bill. Properties that don't sell move to a continued upset sale and a judicial sale in December, both run online through GovEase. The December 8, 2026 lists are posted on the county's Upset and Judicial Sales page.

  • Partial payments of any size are accepted without a written plan.
  • An Agreement to Stay Sale sets quarterly payments over 12 months for owners facing a sale.
  • After June 1 of the sale year, pay by cashier's check or money order. Taxes 18 months delinquent need certified funds.
  • Cash is no longer taken. The Bureau is at 55 East Court Street, 5th floor, and answers at 215-348-6274 from 8:15 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. on weekdays.

Any county, township or school tax debt comes out of the seller's proceeds ahead of other debts, so a lien shrinks the cash you leave with. Before the settlement date, ask the Tax Claim Bureau for a lien certificate using the request form on the county's site. Watch for interim bills as well, since a recent improvement can add a quarterly charge.

The recorder collects a 2% realty transfer tax at recording, split between the state and local governments, and the purchase agreement decides who pays it. Under Act 29, new owners must give the Board of Assessment their contact information within 30 days of buying. A new recorded deed, a refinance included, also ends the homestead exclusion until a fresh application is filed within 45 days.

If you carry tax debt, an expired homestead or a stalled appeal, you can still sell without fixing each item first. A buyer purchasing as-is can close cleanly with the lien paid from proceeds. Get written figures from the Board and the Bureau before you accept any offer.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html: Pull your latest county, township and school bills and check each one against the tax collector's records. Look for any interim bill from a recent improvement. Confirm that the homestead exclusion is active on your primary residence. If you plan to appeal, line up a certified appraisal or recent comparable sales before the deadline, because the hearing notice gives you only 20 days. Then call the Board at 215-348-6219 with any parcel, municipality or school district questions, and request the lien certificate early so the closing agent has it in hand.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Bucks County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Board of Assessment Appeals at 215-348-6219. The office is at 55 East Court Street, 6th floor, Doylestown, open 8:30 a.m. to 4:15 p.m., Monday through Friday. Questions about parcel number, municipality or school district go to the same line.

faqs.q: When is the Bucks County homestead exclusion application due?
faqs.a: The application for the school tax year starting July 1, 2027 is due March 1, 2027. File it with the Board of Assessment Appeals. A new recorded deed, including a refinance, requires a new application within 45 days.

faqs.q: What is the filing fee for a Bucks County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: The fee is $75.00 per parcel and it is non-refundable. It applies to annual and interim residential appeals, and the check is payable to the Bucks County Board of Assessment. Don't mail cash.

faqs.q: How long before Bucks County can sell a house for unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: The Tax Claim Bureau can sell a property once a lien stays unpaid for 18 months. Eligible properties go to the upset sale in September of the second year, and unsold ones can move to the December judicial sale. You can stop a sale by paying before the close of business at the courthouse the day before it.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax when I sell my Bucks County house?
faqs.a: Yes, a 2% realty transfer tax is paid when the deed is recorded, with 1% to the state and 1% to the municipality and school district. The purchase agreement usually divides it between buyer and seller. Exemptions exist for some family transfers.
